definitions: A technique in image processing where the threshold value for binarization is not fixed but varies across different regions of an image.
A method used to separate foreground from background in images, particularly effective for images with uneven illumination, by calculating a local threshold for each pixel or region.
examples: Adaptive Thresholding is crucial for document scanning.
The algorithm uses Adaptive Thresholding to enhance text.
Understanding Adaptive Thresholding improves image segmentation.
